Interesting — the edit tool auto-commits each edit as a "wip(edit)" commit. So the working tree is clean and the changes are committed. That's fine; the answer includes committed files. So my stash test didn't work because there were no uncommitted changes; `git stash push pre_commit/git.py` with no local modifications created nothing.

So to test the regression, I need to revert the fix or check out the previous commit for git.py. Let me use `git show ddd3e26^:pre_commit/git.py` no... The commit ddd3e26 is "wip(edit): pre_commit/git.py" which contains the fix. The parent is 7b88c63. So I can temporarily checkout the old git.py, run the test, then restore.

Let me do: `git show 7b88c63:pre_commit/git.py > pre_commit/git.py` then run test, then `git checkout HEAD -- pre_commit/git.py`. But the edit tool auto-commits... the bash writing won't be committed. Then restore via git checkout. Good.

Wait, but if I modify git.py via bash and then run pytest, that's the un-fixed version. Then restore.
